steps.name: Treated vs control DE (edgeR QLF) + shallow-sample sensitivity
caveats: Do NOT drop sample_01 from the primary analysis: the shallow library inflates its per-gene noise, but TMM normalization keeps it estimable; quantify its influence via the sensitivity re-run instead.
With 6 vs 6 samples, avoid over-filtering. If the padj < 0.05 set is empty, report the top genes by padj and state that no gene passed the FDR threshold — do not silently relax it.
The 12,000 rows are likely a pre-filtered gene set; do not assume whole-transcriptome completeness when interpreting the number of DE genes.
If any helper errors on fractional counts, fix the code path (edgeR accepts non-integers natively); never fall back to rounding.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-without-rsem-counts-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 sample columns; RSEM gene-level expected counts, i.e. fractional) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-rsem-counts-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample id + condition; per the design profile 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch). Known caveat: the per-sample RSEM genes.results files with effective lengths were not delivered, so the matrix's length-correction status is unknown. The row ID space of counts.csv (symbols vs Entrez vs Ensembl) is not documented and must be detected from the file.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the 6 treated and 6 control colon samples, and how robust are those results to the shallow sample_01 (library size ~4x below the median)?
constraints: Model the fractional RSEM expected counts with edgeR's negative-binomial GLM (glmQLFit + glmQLFTest). Do NOT round counts and do NOT use DESeq2/pydeseq2, which require integers.
Normalize with TMM (calcNormFactors). The design is one-way, unpaired, single batch: fit ~ 0 + condition with no batch or other covariates, contrasting treated vs control.
Use the actual condition values from metadata.csv (6 treated vs 6 control per the design profile).

Primary analysis uses all 12 samples. Apply a low-expression filter (keep genes with CPM above a small threshold in at least 6 of the 12 samples) identically in both analyses and report how many genes were removed.
Sensitivity analysis: re-run the identical pipeline with sample_01 removed; report sample_01's condition group from metadata.csv and the resulting group sizes.
Multiple testing: BH-adjusted FDR; primary DE set at padj < 0.05, and additionally list genes with raw p < 0.05 but padj >= 0.05 for reference.
Shrink log2FC with apeglm fitted to the edgeR GLM, and produce the full-gene ranked list (ordered by shrunk log2FC) for downstream GSEA.
Detect the row ID space of counts.csv and keep native IDs in the DE table; also provide an HGNC symbol mapping for downstream use.
State explicitly in the results that the length-correction status of the matrix is unknown (RSEM length files not delivered), so a gene-length bias cannot be ruled out.
steps.description: Primary deliverable: treated vs control DE table on RSEM expected counts (edgeR NB-GLM with QLF, TMM normalization, apeglm LFC shrinkage), per-sample QC documenting sample_01's ~4x library-size deficit, and a sensitivity re-run excluding sample_01 with DE-set overlap quantified.
acceptance_criteria: A DE table with one row per gene (all 12,000 input genes) containing log2FC, raw P, padj (BH), shrunk log2FC, and a count/expression summary, produced for both the all-12 analysis and the 11-sample analysis without sample_01.
DE gene sets at padj < 0.05 for both analyses, plus the Jaccard overlap of the two DE sets and an explicit list of genes gained or lost (with fold-change direction) when sample_01 is excluded.
Per-sample QC: raw library sizes, TMM size factors, and an explicit statement of sample_01's deviation from the median library size.
PCA plot (first 2 PCs) colored by condition and an MA plot of the treated vs control contrast, as image files.
sample_01's condition group (treated or control) reported from metadata.csv.

steps.name: Pathway context: GSEA + GO on DE genes (human)
caveats: If the padj < 0.05 DE set is small or empty, GO over-representation is underpowered — report the GSEA results as the primary functional readout and say so explicitly.
WikiPathways GMT lines carry '%'-delimited descriptors; split on '%' so output carries readable set names.
This step is supplementary: a failed or empty enrichment result does not invalidate the T1S1 DE conclusions.
steps.context: Consumes T1S1 outputs: the full-gene ranked list ordered by apeglm-shrunk log2FC, and the padj < 0.05 DE sets (up-only, down-only). Provisioned human references: a WikiPathways human GMT (HGNC symbols, descriptor split on '%') in the reference store, and the local org.Hs.eg.db / GO.db annotation packages for symbol mapping and GO enrichment. The dataset is Homo sapiens; the mouse and rat WikiPathways collections must not be used.
steps.question: Which pathways and biological processes are enriched among genes up- or down-regulated by treatment?
constraints: Run GSEA with fgsea on the ranked list (ordered by shrunk log2FC, directional) against the human WikiPathways GMT, with BH FDR within the assay.
Run GO over-representation (clusterProfiler, offline against local org.Hs.eg.db + GO.db) separately on the up-only, down-only, and combined padj < 0.05 DE sets.

First map T1S1's gene ID space to HGNC symbols via org.Hs.eg.db (fall back to the provisioned UniProt human ID-mapping table if needed); report the number and fraction of genes unmapped and continue with the mapped subset.
Use only the human reference data; do not use the mouse or rat pathway collections.
steps.description: Supplementary functional context: fgsea GSEA against the provisioned human WikiPathways GMT on the shrunk-log2FC ranked list, and GO over-representation (up/down/combined) on the DE gene sets, all on HGNC-mapped human symbols.
acceptance_criteria: GSEA results table (WikiPathways sets, human): top up- and down-enriched sets with NES, nominal P, and FDR; the number of sets reaching FDR < 0.25 is reported.
GO enrichment tables (BP, CC, MF) for the up, down, and combined DE sets with BH-adjusted P values.
A statement of gene-ID mapping success: how many genes mapped to HGNC symbols and how many were unmapped.

plan.title: Colon treated vs control DE on RSEM expected counts
plan.analytical_narrative: Two-step analysis of the delivered human colon bulk RNA-seq dataset: RSEM gene-level expected counts in counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples, fractional values) plus a 12-row condition table in metadata.csv (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), with sample_01 ~4x below-median library size. Because the counts are fractional, integer-requiring models (DESeq2, pydeseq2) are ruled out; edgeR's negative-binomial GLM with quasi-likelihood F-testing models non-integer counts natively, and its TMM library-size normalization keeps the shallow sample_01 estimable rather than forcing an ad hoc exclusion. T1S1 therefore runs per-sample QC (library sizes, TMM factors, PCA, MA), a one-way GLM (treated vs control), BH FDR, apeglm LFC shrinkage for a ranked list, and a sensitivity re-run with sample_01 removed, reporting how the DE set changes. T1S2 then adds functional context — fgsea GSEA against the provisioned human WikiPathways GMT and GO over-representation via local org.Hs.eg.db/GO.db on the significant DE sets — after mapping the matrix's row ID space to HGNC symbols. The primary deliverable is the DE table with the shallow-sample sensitivity comparison; enrichment is supplementary.
